context.description: Mount Remarkable National Park rises above the Willochra Plain at the southern end of the Flinders Ranges, 45 km north of Port Pirie. Walking tracks lead to a 960 m summit and through gorges cut into ancient rock, and valley trails are home to echidnas and lace monitors. The Willowie trails and the Remarkable Epic trail draw mountain bikers, and Melrose, the oldest town in the Flinders Ranges, sits at the foot of the mountain.

context.description: The Southern Flinders Ranges is the southernmost tourism region of the Flinders and Outback, running from Spalding and Yacka in the south to Orroroo and Carrieton in the north. Port Pirie and Port Germein mark its western edge and Peterborough its eastern. Its small towns hold heritage museums, art galleries, craft breweries and bakeries, with the Heysen and Mawson trails and the Southern Flinders Rail Trail running through.

context.description: Leigh Creek is the gateway town to the northern Flinders Ranges, 540 km north of Adelaide. Its coalfield closed in 2015, and the dam beside it is now used for kayaking and fishing. Around it are the stone township of Beltana, the sculptures and ochre pits at Lyndhurst, and Nilpena Ediacara National Park, where guided tours reach a field of early animal fossils.

context.description: Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges National Park was proclaimed in 1970 on the traditional country of the Adnyamathanha people. Its gorge hikes and 4WD tracks cross rugged ranges, reaching the edge of Lake Frome, an ephemeral salt lake about 100 km long. Arkaroola Wilderness Sanctuary, a 610 sq km private reserve beside the park, is the main visitor base. In 2023 it was certified as South Australia's first International Dark Sky Sanctuary.
